title: Multi-dimensional breakpoint and degraded-model routing
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Implement a multi-dimensional circuit guard that evaluates multiple SLO-aligned signals (error rate, latency percentiles, error-budget burn rate, and token-queue depth) and safely routes affected traffic to progressively degraded model paths with strong tenant isolation and observability. This ticket covers design, runtime implementation, canary rollout, and operational runbook additions.
background_and_motivation: We frequently see incidents where single-signal breakers (errors or p99 alone) either over-eject healthy tenants or react too late when combined signals indicate systemic stress. Customers running mixed workloads (short chat vs long-generation pipelines) require finer control so a single noisy tenant doesn't trigger wide-ranging fallbacks. We want an approach that: 1) combines signals to make robust decisions, 2) supports per-tenant and per-model policies, 3) provides safe degraded-model routing (quantized or smaller variants) before cross-region failover, and 4) keeps traceability for debugging and billing reconciliation.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes a configurable circuit-guard policy engine with at least four input signals: error_rate, p99_latency, error_budget_burn_rate, token_queue_depth
Policies support per-tenant and per-model overrides and inherit sensible defaults from global config
When guard trips, traffic is routed to a pre-configured degraded path (model variant or cached-response) with preserved request semantics and KV cache compatibility where feasible
Hysteresis windows and cooldowns prevent oscillation (configurable sliding window with min 30s and cooldown default 5m)
Metrics emitted: guard_state (OPEN/DEGRADED/CLOSED), reason_tags, fallback_success, fallback_latency_penalty, per-tenant_fallback_rate
Integration tests simulate mixed workloads and validate no more than 10% collateral degradation to non-impacted tenants under a noisy tenant spike
Canary rollout plan documented and executed with automated rollback on >5% increase in global p99 or >10% failed degraded fallbacks
Runbook updated and on-call playbook verified in chaos rehearsal
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Combined-signal decision: use weighted scoring of normalized signals rather than Boolean AND/OR to allow graceful sensitivity tuning

Fallback hierarchy: prefer intra-region degraded-models (quantized / smaller-arch) -> cached prefix responses -> regional failover. Cross-region failover is last resort to avoid cross-az egress costs and compliance issues
State management: lightweight in-memory guard state per serving node with durable publish to central telemetry for auditing. Avoid heavy distributed consensus to keep latency SLOs
Hysteresis parameters: choose sliding windows (1m/5m) and cooldowns to balance detection speed vs flapping. Will tune with traffic replay

KV cache compatibility: where model variants change tokenizer or embedding dimensions, we avoid transparent fallback unless an adapter exists — prefer cached-response or model-variant with conversion shim for session continuity
Per-tenant vs global policy: default global policy with per-tenant policy stored in config service. Tenants above reserved tier can opt into stricter isolation (no cross-tenant mitigation)
implementation_plan: 1. Policy engine: add scoring engine module (runtime/policy/score_engine.go) with pluggable signal adapters
2. Signals: wire up telemetry to export error_rate (1m/5m), latency percentiles, token_queue_depth, and error-budget burn rate from rate-limiter module
3. Fallback adapters: implement degraded-model router that supports model variants, cached-prefix fallbacks, and queued-defer with client-visible retry headers
4. State & telemetry: emit guard_state events to tracing and prometheus and log reason_tags to central logging
5. Tests: local load-sim harness with synthetic tenants and long-tail jobs; add unit tests for scoring and integration tests for routing correctness
6. Canary: deploy to region-staging then to 10% of production traffic with circuit-breaker feature flag per-service
7. Runbook: add step-by-step mitigation and rollback instructions; coordinate with SRE and support
milestones: 2026-02-17: Policy engine prototype and unit tests (PR #4123)
2026-03-04: Degraded-model router first-pass and compatibility shim
risks_and_mitigation: Oscillation / flapping: mitigated by conservative default hysteresis and cross-node consensus backoff (leader-elected cooloff for global actions)
Collateral degradation to non-impacted tenants: we simulate multi-tenant contention and enforce per-tenant caps on fallback blast radius
Fallback model quality regressions: require per-fallback evaluation sets and automated quality gates before enabling for any tenant marked critical
Billing reconciliation complexity: add explicit audit events for each routed fallback request to attribute token usage correctly
testing_and_validation: Chaos test: PID-based sinatra test that spikes token_queue_depth for one tenant and verifies other tenants maintain SLO
Replay traffic: run 24h replay with production traces in staging to tune weights and hysteresis
A/B experiment: 5% traffic uses new guard, compare p99/error-rate and fallback-success metrics
Quality regression: run fallback outputs through existing eval harness and ensure <2% semantic regression on critical prompts
rollout_plan: Start in staging -> region-staging -> 10% prod -> 50% prod -> 100% prod
Each step requires 72h observation window and signoff from SRE and product
Automated rollback triggers: >5% increase global p99 OR >10% failed fallbacks OR >2x expected cost increase over 1h
dashboards_and_alerting: Guard Overview dashboard: per-region/tenant guard_state, fallback_rate, fallback_latency_penalty
Guard Health alert: sustained guard_state == DEGRADED for >10m in >5% nodes
Fallback Failure alert: >1% fallback failure rate for 15m
Cost spike alert: fallback_cost delta > 30% over baseline for 1h
